text:
maya: Seeing a 503 spike on kube-apiserver in us-central1 starting ~2024-05-14 09:12 UTC. Errors align with attach/onboard traffic from gpu provisioning. Socket wait high, SYN backlog growing. Any insight?
ops-bot: [alert] apiserver.high_503_rate us-central1 — incident INC-4821 created — paging eng-sre
chris: jumping on it — fd_count on amb-proxies at 95%. nat ephemeral ports ~88% used. Lots of short-lived connections from attach-runner jobs.
anita: Confirmed: onboarding batch jobs ramped 3x at 09:10 (autoscaler triggered). They open ~10 conns per attach attempt. Retries are amplifying.
leo: If NAT ports are the bottleneck, we can (1) increase proxy conn limit, (2) enable conn reuse on attach clients, or (3) limit onboarding concurrency. Tradeoffs: (1) costs more infra, (2) needs client change, (3) delays onboarding.
maya: Pausing the onboarding ramp now. @platform can we bump proxy conn_limit and restart amb-proxy in us-central1? If a config change is quick, do it.
chris: quick check — apiserver logs show repeated 502/503 with "connection refused" from proxy due to ephemeral exhaustion. Running:
```
kubectl -n infra logs deploy/amb-proxy-usc -c proxy | grep -E "SYN|port"
```
anita: suggestion — add short-term NAT scaling: spin up extra NAT gateways and route proxy traffic through them. Might avoid changing clients.
leo: Platform note: NAT IP quota is tight in us-central1, taking more requires cloud quota request (~24h). Proxy conn_limit bump is faster but we'll hit OS fd limits on proxy nodes unless we increase ulimits.
maya: I'm going to apply a config bump: proxy.conn_limit 20000 -> 30000 and restart pods, and also set graceful_conn_reuse=true for 48h. Rolling now.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: config commit 0f4a9e — rolling restart amb-proxy-usc (3 pods) — started by maya
chris: Restart done on two pods, one pending due to image pull, fallback routed to other proxies, watching metrics.
maya: Metrics: SYN backlog falling, apiserver 503 rate down 70% in 2m :thumbsup: 
anita: Resuming onboarding at 09:40 UTC with throttling (concurrency x0.5). Will monitor controller-manager queue latencies — retries might cause watch fanout.
leo: Let's add a follow-up action: (A) spike-protection for onboarder (b) connection pooling client change (c) infra runbook update about NAT quotas. Filing follow-ups in INC-4821.
maya: Good. Closing incident in 30m if stable. Thanks all.
ops-bot: incident INC-4821 status: acknowledged -> mitigated by maya — tags: apiserver, nat, gpu-onboard
